This makes it easy to pass synthetic data directly to competing-risks estimators and metrics. ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A multi-state `Surv` response ready for use with `AalenJohansen`, `FineGray`, or any competing-risks metric. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariate matrix of shape `(n, n_covariates)`, or `None` when `n_covariates=0`. [latent_times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Per-cause latent event times of shape `(n, n_causes)` before the competing-risks minimum is taken. Useful for constructing oracle predictions in tests and benchmarks. [censoring_time]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Array]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The censoring time for each subject, shape `(n,)`. The observed time is `min(min(latent_times, axis=1), censoring_time)`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Generate synthetic competing-risks data with two causes and three covariates. The result holds a ready-to-use `Surv` response and covariate matrix: ::: {#a33d4cd0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw sim = gw.simulate_competing_risks( n=500, n_causes=2, n_covariates=3, seed=42 ) sim.surv ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Surv(type=mright, n=500, events=296, states=('cause1', 'cause2')) ``` ::: ::: The covariates and latent times are available for oracle comparisons: ::: {#1fdbfba8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sim.covariates.shape, sim.latent_times.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ((500, 3), (500, 2)) ``` ::: :::
